questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Final Velocity of a Particle
questions.problem: The initial velocity of a particle is $(5i+3j)\,\text{m/s}.$ Find the speed of the particle after $3$ seconds if the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(-i+2j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
u=5i+3j,\,a=-i+2j.
$$

Therefore, after $3$ seconds, the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(5i+3j)+(-i+2j)(3) \\  & =(5i+3j)+(-3i+6j) \\  & =(2i+9j)\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the speed of the particle is

$$
\begin{aligned}|v| & =|2i+9j| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{9}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+81} \\  & =\sqrt{85} \\  & ≈9.22\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Acceleration of a Particle
questions.problem: A particle moves with constant acceleration. When $t=0\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $(5i+j)\,\text{ft/s},$ and when $t=4\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $(5i+13j)\,\text{ft/s}.$ Calculate the acceleration of the particle.
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=5i+j,\,v=5i+13j,\,t=4,
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $a,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 5i+13j & =(5i+j)+a(4) \\ 12j & =4a \\ a & =\frac{1}{4}(12j) \\  & =3j\,{\text{ft/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

u=-4i+9j,\,v=-4i+9j,\,t=7

questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
u=2i+5j,\,a=-3i+j.
$$

Therefore, after $t=3\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(2i+5j)+(-3i+j)(3) \\  & =(2i+5j)+(-9i+3j) \\  & =(-7\,i+8\,j)\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the speed of the particle is

$$
\begin{aligned}|v| & =|-7i+8j| \\  & =\sqrt{(-7)^{2}+{8}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{49+64} \\  & =\sqrt{113}\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Time when a Particle Reaches a Particular Velocity
questions.problem:
A particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(-2i+4j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}.$ The velocity of the particle is $(10i-8j)\,\text{km/h}$ when $t=0\,\text{h}.$ Find the time when the velocity of the particle equals $(-8i+28j)\,\text{km/h}.$

$t=$
{{field-1}}$\,\text{h}$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=10i-8j,\,v=-8i+28j,\,a=-2i+4j,
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ -8i+28j & =10i-8j+(-2i+4j)t \\ -18i+36j & =(-2i+4j)t \\ -18i+36j & =-2ti+4tj\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the $i$ and $j$ components in the last equation, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}-18=-2t \\ 36=4t\end{aligned}\,⟹\,t=9\,\text{h}.
$$
